name: Small white butterfly
description: A pale, fluttering butterfly that drifts from flower to flower.

facts.text: Feeds on nectar from open, sunny flowers.
Rests with its wings closed, showing their pale green-grey undersides.
More flowering patches mean more butterflies at once.

hints.text: Something pale and fluttering might come to flowers in bloom.

name: Swallowtail butterfly
description: A large, striking butterfly with tailed hindwings. An uncommon visitor.

facts.text: Only visits gardens with plenty of flowers in bloom.
Its tailed hindwings give the swallowtail its name.

hints.text: A rarer butterfly might visit a garden that is full of flowers.

name: Bumblebee
description: A round, fuzzy bee that hums steadily between flowers.

facts.text: Arrives once a couple of flower patches are in bloom.
Carries pollen between flowers as it feeds.

hints.text: A humming visitor may come once more than one patch is in flower.

name: Ground beetle
description: A glossy, dark beetle that keeps to damp, sheltered places.

facts.text: Moves into natural shelters that are shaded and surrounded by cover.
Spends most of its time hidden, venturing out to forage nearby.
In an insect hotel it tucks in for long rests, as beetles do to see out the winter in hollow stems and dead wood.

hints.text: Something small might hide in a shady pile of logs and leaves.
A shelter in shade, with plants close around it, suits ground beetles.

name: Wren
description: A tiny brown bird with a cocked tail and a surprisingly loud song.

facts.text: Visits well-placed, improved shelters, where it finds cover and a place to nest.
Comes to gardens already busy with insects, a sign that there is plenty for a small bird.
Wrens often build nests in log piles and dense cover.

hints.text: An improved shelter in a garden busy with butterflies, bees and beetles might tempt a small bird.
Wrens visit improved shelters in good spots, and love a nesting bundle.

name: Japanese white-eye
description: A small olive-green songbird with a bright white ring around each eye.

facts.text: Comes to gardens with established bamboo, where it rests and preens out of the wind.
A mature maple nearby makes it a more frequent visitor.
White-eyes often travel in pairs, chattering softly to each other.
In the court it drinks nectar from camellia flowers.

hints.text: Some songbirds like tall, dense growth to rest in.
Two or more mature bamboo clumps might draw a small green songbird.
A mature maple near the bamboo makes white-eyes visit more often.

name: Red admiral
description: A velvety black butterfly with bold red bands and white wing tips.

facts.text: Feeds on tree sap and fallen fruit as well as nectar.
Often basks with its wings spread flat in the sun.

hints.text: Not every butterfly feeds on nectar. Some prefer sap.
A sap feeder filled with maple sap draws the red admiral.

name: Mason bee
description: A small, gentle solitary bee that seals its nest tubes with mud.

facts.text: Nests in hollow canes, one egg chamber after another.
Solitary bees rarely sting; there is no hive for them to defend.

hints.text: Hollow canes could make homes for a solitary insect.
An insect hotel, built from a shelter, is where mason bees nest.

name: Wood mouse
description: A bright-eyed mouse with big ears and a long tail, busy after dark.

facts.text: Stores seeds and nuts in hidden larders near its nest.
Prefers dense cover; it seldom crosses open ground.

hints.text: A deep, dry lodge of logs might suit a small mammal.
A log lodge, built from a shelter, draws wood mice.

name: Common darter
description: A slim red dragonfly that perches, darts out, and returns to the same stem.

facts.text: Comes to ponds with tall reeds and rushes to perch on.
It returns again and again to a favourite perch.

hints.text: Tall stems at the water’s edge make good perches.
Two or more mature reeds or rushes may bring a dragonfly.

name: Pond skater
description: A long-legged insect that glides over the water’s surface.

facts.text: Water-repellent hairs on its feet let it stand on the surface.
It rests in the calm water between lily pads.

hints.text: Calm water between floating leaves suits a small skating insect.

name: Japanese tree frog
description: A tiny bright green frog with a big voice on summer evenings.

facts.text: Comes to ponds already busy with insect life.
It shelters in cool, damp places close to the water.
Sticky toe pads let it climb reeds and leaves.

hints.text: A damp shelter by a pond full of life might tempt a small frog.
Frogs come to a frog shelter once dragonflies or pond skaters are about.

name: Japanese carpenter ant
description: A large black ant that nests in dry crevices and dead wood.

facts.text: Nests in dry, warm crevices between stones.
Ants keep busy trails between their nest and food.

hints.text: A warm, dry crevice might become a nest.

name: Jumping spider
description: A tiny, big-eyed spider that leaps between sunny perches.

facts.text: Basks on sunlit stones and thyme.
It sees remarkably well for its size.

hints.text: Warm stones and low plants in the sun suit a small leaping spider.

name: Japanese grass lizard
description: A slender brown lizard with a very long tail, quick in the sun.

facts.text: Comes to gardens already busy with small life among the stones.
It basks on warm stones to heat up in the morning.
Its tail can be three times the length of its body.

hints.text: A cairn warmed by the sun might draw a basking reptile.
Lizards come to a sun-warmed cairn once ants or spiders are about.

name: Woodlouse
description: A small grey armoured creature of damp, rotting places.

facts.text: Lives in a leaf-litter bed, breaking leaves down into soil.
It is a crustacean, a land-living cousin of crabs.

hints.text: A bed of rotting leaves might draw small decomposers.

name: Millipede
description: A slow, many-legged creature that curls into a spiral when touched.

facts.text: Feeds on rotting leaves and wood.
Despite the name, most have far fewer than a thousand legs.

name: Japanese common toad
description: A broad, warty toad that spends the day tucked into damp leaf litter.

facts.text: Comes to a hollow already busy with life in the leaf litter.
It shelters in deep, damp leaves through the day.

hints.text: A deep, damp leaf bed might hide something larger.
Toads come to a deep leaf bed once woodlice and millipedes live there.

name: Hoverfly
description: A wasp-striped fly that hangs in the air above flowers.

facts.text: Visits meadows with more than one kind of flower.
Its stripes copy a wasp’s, but it cannot sting.

hints.text: A meadow with several kinds of flower draws more kinds of visitor.

name: Mining bee
description: A small furry bee that digs its nest in bare earth.

facts.text: Nests in a bee bank in a meadow already busy with pollinators.
Each female digs her own small burrow.

hints.text: Some bees dig their nests in bare, sunny earth.

name: Meadow grasshopper
description: A green grasshopper that chirps from the long grass.

facts.text: Comes where several clumps of tall grass grow.
It sings by rubbing its legs against its wings.

hints.text: Long grass in the sun suits a singing insect.

name: Hummingbird hawk-moth
description: A day-flying moth that hovers like a tiny hummingbird.

facts.text: Comes only to meadows with many kinds of flower in bloom.
It hovers while it feeds, its wings a blur.

hints.text: A meadow rich in different flowers might bring a rare hovering moth.

name: Banded demoiselle
description: A metallic blue damselfly with dark bands on its wings.

facts.text: Rests on iris and sedge beside moving water.
It flutters more than it flies, like a butterfly.

hints.text: Tall leaves beside the stream make perches for a jewel-bright insect.

name: Mayfly
description: A delicate insect with upright wings and long tail threads.

facts.text: Gathers where the banks are well planted.
A mayfly lives most of its life as a nymph in the stream.

hints.text: Plant the banks well, and delicate stream insects may gather.

name: Grey wagtail
description: A slim grey and lemon-yellow bird that bobs its long tail.

facts.text: Comes to streams busy with insects, and stands on stones in the water.
It bobs its tail constantly as it walks.

hints.text: Stones to stand on in the stream might bring a water-loving bird.
Wagtails stand on stepping and resting stones once stream insects are about.

name: Brown-eared bulbul
description: A noisy grey bird with chestnut cheeks and a fondness for fruit.

facts.text: Comes to a fruit table set with quince.
Bulbuls carry fruit seeds far across the sanctuary.

hints.text: A fruit-loving bird might visit if fruit were set out.

name: Japanese bush warbler
description: A plain olive bird with one of the loveliest songs in Japan.

facts.text: Sings from blossom in a court already busy with insects.
Its song, “hō-hokekyo”, announces spring.

hints.text: A songbird might sing from blossoming branches.

name: Carpenter bee
description: A big, glossy black bee with yellow fur, gentle and slow.

facts.text: Comes where several kinds of shrub are in flower.
It nests by tunnelling into dry wood.

name: Varied tit
description: A bold little tit with chestnut flanks and a cream face.

facts.text: Nests in tree holes and nest boxes in shaded woodland.
It stores acorns and seeds to find later.

hints.text: A hole-nesting bird might move into a nest box.

name: Stag beetle
description: A large, gentle beetle with antler-like jaws.

facts.text: Its young live for years inside rotting wood.
The “antlers” are only for show and wrestling.

hints.text: More deadwood on the ground might bring a large beetle.

name: Japanese dormouse
description: A tiny tree-dwelling dormouse with a dark stripe down its back.

facts.text: Lives in a dormouse box in woodland already full of life.
It is protected as a natural monument in Japan.

hints.text: A nest box turned towards the trunk suits a tiny climber.

name: Japanese pipistrelle
description: A small bat that flits around the canopy at dusk.

facts.text: A rare visitor that roosts in a bat box near a garden busy with insects.
It finds its way in the dark by listening to echoes.

hints.text: A narrow box open at the bottom might shelter something that flies at dusk.
Bats are rare; they roost in a bat box once insects are plentiful.

name: Oriental reed warbler
description: A loud brown warbler that sings from the top of a reed stem.

facts.text: Sings from dense reed beds in a marsh already busy with insects.
It weaves its nest between upright reed stems.

hints.text: A dense reed bed might bring a loud little singer.

name: Moorhen
description: A dark waterbird with a red bill, picking its way among floating leaves.

facts.text: Comes to pools with floating leaves to walk on.
Its long toes spread its weight on soft leaves and mud.

hints.text: Floating leaves on open pools suit a long-toed waterbird.

name: Brimstone butterfly
description: A sulphur-yellow butterfly, one of the first out in spring.

facts.text: Visits in spring, as soon as early flowers open.
It spends the winter tucked in evergreen leaves.

hints.text: Some butterflies come only in spring.

name: Seven-spot ladybird
description: A bright red beetle with seven black spots.

facts.text: In autumn and winter it gathers in sheltered places to see out the cold.
Ladybirds cluster together through the winter.

hints.text: A shelter in this garden might hold winter guests when the cold comes.

name: Eurasian bullfinch
description: A plump finch with a rosy breast and a soft, piping call.

facts.text: Comes in autumn and winter for berries and buds.
Pairs of bullfinches stay together all year.

hints.text: Berries and buds through the cold months might bring a winter bird.

name: Golden dragonfly
description: A dragonfly that shines like gold leaf over still water. Few have ever seen one.

facts.text: A rare visitor to a well-planted pond already full of dragonflies.
It never comes on a schedule; a suitable pond is all it asks.

hints.text: A rare dragonfly is said to visit the Noble Garden’s pond when it is at its best.
Flowering lotus and dragonflies already on the pond make it more likely.
